package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sync"

	machine "github.com/whitaker-io/machine/v4"
)

// Order is the payload the looping flow carries. Attempt is what MAKES THE LOOP
// TERMINATE: it rises by one on every pass, and the branch predicate reads it.
type Order struct {
	ID      string
	Attempt int
}

// attemptsBeforeDone is how many passes the datum makes before the branch routes
// it out of the loop. The token asserts on this exact number, so a loop that ran
// the wrong number of times fails rather than passing quietly.
const attemptsBeforeDone = 3

// loopCapacity buffers the one datum plus its re-entries, so a Send back into the
// edge never blocks the node that issued it.
const loopCapacity = attemptsBeforeDone + 1

// Feed is the source transport. It pushes exactly ONE datum, so the attempt count
// the token carries is unambiguously the loop's work rather than an artifact of
// several data racing.
//
// IT MINTS DATA WITH machine.RebuildPacket, which is the exported packet
// constructor: there is no exported path from a Frame to a Packet, so this is the
// sanctioned way for a transport to produce one.
func Feed() machine.EdgeFactory[Order] {
	return func(node string, report machine.Report) (machine.Edge[Order], error) {
		return &feedEdge{node: node, ch: make(chan machine.Packet[Order], loopCapacity)}, nil
	}
}

type feedEdge struct {
	node string
	ch   chan machine.Packet[Order]
	once sync.Once
}

func (e *feedEdge) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
	e.once.Do(func() {
		packet, err := machine.RebuildPacket(machine.FrameData{
			ID:     "datum-0",
			Source: e.node,
			Node:   e.node,
		}, Order{ID: "order-0"})
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		e.ch <- packet
	})

	return nil
}

// Send is what the LOOP exercises. The generated Wire calls hold.Send(ingest), so
// every re-entry arrives here and goes back onto the same channel the source
// reads from.
func (e *feedEdge) Send(ctx context.Context, packet machine.Packet[Order]) error {
	select {
	case e.ch <- packet:
		return nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}

func (e *feedEdge) Receive() <-chan machine.Packet[Order] { return e.ch }

func (e *feedEdge) Close() error { return nil }

// Bump raises the datum's attempt counter. It is the loop's progress: without it
// the branch below would route the same way forever.
func Bump(f machine.Frame[Order]) Order {
	out := f.Value()
	out.Attempt++

	return out
}

// Done is the branch predicate and the loop's TERMINATION CONDITION. True routes
// the datum to finished and out of the loop; false routes it to retrying, which
// is the outlet the send re-enters from.
func Done(f machine.Frame[Order]) bool { return f.Value().Attempt >= attemptsBeforeDone }

// Hold is the node the retrying outlet feeds and the one the send re-enters from.
// It changes nothing: the construct under test is the re-entry, not a transform.
func Hold(f machine.Frame[Order]) Order { return f.Value() }

// Report is the sink. It prints the LOCKED TOKEN from the fixture's own code,
// carrying the attempt count the loop produced.
func Report(f machine.Frame[Order]) Order {
	v := f.Value()
	Emit(v.Attempt)

	return v
}

// done is closed once the token has been printed, so main can exit on the datum
// rather than on a timer.
var done = make(chan struct{})

var emitOnce sync.Once

// Emit prints the locked token. The harness asserts on the running program's
// stdout, so nothing but the flow actually looping and then leaving the loop can
// produce it.
func Emit(attempt int) {
	emitOnce.Do(func() {
		fmt.Printf("flow-loop: attempts=%d\n", attempt)
		close(done)
	})
}
